newsitem.title: USA: U.S. wants separate Taiwan, China WTO accessions.
newsitem.headline: U.S. wants separate Taiwan, China WTO accessions.

text.p: The United States believes that Taiwan's accession to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) should be independent of China's, according to a letter released on Tuesday.

"Regarding WTO accession for Taiwan and the Peoples Republic of China, administration policy is that each accession will be judged on its own merits," U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said in the letter.
The letter, dated February 13, was addressed to California Republican Representative Chris Cox, who released it to the media.
"I am delighted to see that the administration has unambiguously de-linked Taiwan's entry into the WTO from communist China's entry," Cox said in an accompanying statement.
At a WTO meeting in Geneva last Friday on Taiwan's accession, trade officials said Taipei's application seemed to be unavoidably linked to China's.
China, which regards Taiwan as a renegade province, has said it would accept Taiwan's membership in the WTO as a customs territory -- but only after China itself is admitted.
Barshefsky's letter said all WTO accessions, including those of the People's Republic of China and Taiwan, should be based on commercial, not political criteria.
She said that, although progress had been made with Taiwan, a number of issues remained unresolved, including trade barriers on key U.S. farm products.
"The United States supports Taiwan's accession to the WTO -- but, as with other applicants for membership, only on commercially meaningful terms," Barshefsky wrote.
